flags.why: The common first-person use of bác when speaking to someone who calls you bác is missing. [Dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/bác)
flags.fix: pron | I, me (an uncle, aunt or older adult speaking to someone who addresses them as bác)

flags.why: The kinship meaning includes an elder brother or sister of either parent, rather than only the father's elder brother. [Dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/bác)
flags.fix: uncle; aunt (an elder brother or sister of either parent)

flags.why: The example explains what bác means instead of using it to refer to someone.
flags.fix: Bác tôi đến thăm nhà hôm qua. = My uncle came to visit yesterday.

flags.why: Bác trứng means cooking eggs over gentle heat, not beating raw eggs before cooking. [Dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/bác)
flags.fix: to scramble (eggs, by cooking over gentle heat)

flags.why: The example incorrectly uses bác for beating eggs in a bowl.
flags.fix: Mẹ đang bác trứng trong chảo. = Mum is scrambling eggs in the pan.

flags.why: Thầy meaning a teacher or respected instructor remains current, including in the quoted proverb. [Dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/thầy)
Nàng for a young woman belongs primarily to literary language, which the endearing tag does not convey. [Dictionary](https://loigiaihay.com/tu-dien-tv/nang-ezkHGPAeYkkCd.html)
Nàng tiên cá means a mermaid generally and does not by itself specify the Little Mermaid.
Yên meaning peaceful or calm is also ordinary spoken Vietnamese. [Dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/yên)
Bàn thắng means a goal, but thắng itself does not mean goal or score.
The example naturally uses thường in its everyday habitual meaning and does not demonstrate the archaic sense 'once; formerly'.
Chả includes grilled or fried pieces of meat or seafood, so restricting it to ground-food patties excludes common uses. [Dictionary](https://vi.wiktionary.org/wiki/chả)
flags.fix: a grilled or fried dish made from seasoned meat, seafood or eggs, in pieces or minced

flags.why: This pronoun is current in casual Southern speech and is misleadingly marked rare. [Dictionary](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/chả)
